header: This is THE people worker, rebuilt entirely on `employee_roster` (Stage 8). It REPLACES the old queryPeople() in analytics.ts, which queried public."user"/public.departments directly and sorted by a parsed ticket number. That was confirmed (chat, 28 Sep 2026) to be the root cause of every "wrong seniority order" bug found this session. Design notes, decided in chat:
- employee_roster.{name, designation_grade_id, sail_department_id, global_seniority_rank} are AUTHORITATIVE: I read them directly, never from public."user", until the next roster refresh.
- public."user" is joined ONLY for contactNo/email (the masked-reveal CUG feature), which the roster does not carry.
- I use er.cohort ('executive' | 'nonexecutive') directly for broad exec/nonexec/combined-employee filtering; it is simpler and more robust than deriving it from designation_grade.track.

- 3 of 6,493 roster rows have user_id IS NULL (confirmed: transferred-out executives, not a data bug). The LEFT JOIN means they still appear in lists/counts with name/designation/department but no contact fields; they would already be unreachable via login/reveal anyway.
- My rule: the sort is ALWAYS `ORDER BY er.global_seniority_rank ASC`, no exceptions, no ticketNo fallback. This is the one rule I call "no-compromise."

members.name: namePredicate
doc: Compositional name search (REPLACED 29 Sep 2026). I decided the old flat `mode`+`excludePositions` scheme was itself a form of patchwork: a new enum value/field was needed for every new logical combination a question could express. Now there is a small set of primitives (wordEquals/wordIsFirst/wordIsLast/substring/fuzzy) combined via AND/OR/NOT, which composes for free; see namePredicate.ts. The LLM orchestrator (queryOrchestrator.ts) sets it; the deterministic parser path continues to use the simpler nameFragment/nameExact fields above, unaffected.
